data.name: Sephirra
data.short_meaning: Sephira, from the Hebrew word sepher, meaning 'scroll' or 'book'
data.long_meaning: In the Bible, Sephira is a name given to the Goddess of Wisdom and the Earth, also known as the Queen of Sheba. She is depicted as a woman of great beauty, wealth, and wisdom, who travels to meet King Solomon to test him with her knowledge and understanding. Sephira represents the feminine aspect of the divine, the nurturing and earthly wisdom, and the balance between the material and spiritual worlds.
data.spiritual_meaning: Sephira symbolizes the deep, earthly wisdom and the balance between the material and spiritual worlds.
data.numerology_meaning: A name with a strong intuitive and emotional foundation. It is a name for those who are naturally mystical and have a deep connection with the spiritual world.

in_hebrew.name: ספירה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: ספירה היא שם שמקורו בעברית ומשמעותו היא "אוצר, ספיר". על פי המסורת, השם נאסף מהמילה "ספיר" שמשמעותה "אוצר". השם התפרסם בעקבות חז"ל, שאמר: "ספירה - אוצר". בברית החדשה, השם נשמע בהקשר של "צופים". השם נושא משמעות רבה ביהדות, כמו גם בנצרות. בנוסף, השם נושא חשיבות רבה באסטרונומיה ובמדע.

in_greek.name: Σηφίρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Σηφίρα είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από τις ελληνικές λέξεις "αστέρες" και "στίχοι". Η λέξη "Σηφίρα" έχει σχέση με την αστρονομία και την αριθμητική. Ο ορισμός της λέξης προέρχεται από την προφορά της λέξης "Σηφίρα" ως "Σηφίρα". Η λέξη χρησιμοποιείται επίσης σε εβραϊκά και αραμαϊκά κείμενα. Στην Καινή Διαθήκη, ο ορισμός της λέξης είναι συνδεδεμένος με την αστρονομία και το σύμπαν.

in_latin.name: Sephirra
in_latin.long_meaning: Sephirra est nomen Hebraicum, quod significat "astra, numeri, stellae". Origo nominis est in lingua Hebraica, ubi significat "astra, numeri, stellae". In Scriptura Hebraica, nomen Sephirra conectitur ad numerum et stellas. In ecclesia Christiana, nomen Sephirra habet significatum profundum in spirituali mundo humano.

in_english.name: Sephirra
in_english.long_meaning: Sephirra is a name of Hebrew origin, derived from the Hebrew words "Sevir" and "Keseph," meaning 'heavenly, numbering, celestial bodies.' In biblical context, the name Sephirra appears in association with the concept of numbering and celestial bodies. In Christian tradition, the name Sephirra holds significant meaning in the spiritual world of humanity, representing a connection to the divine and the cosmic order.

data.cultural_impact: Sephira's name has been mentioned in various religious and spiritual traditions, beyond the Christian context. In Kabbalah, Sephirah is one of the ten divine attributes or sefirot, representing the maternal aspect of God. In Gnosticism, the world soul, the Sophia, is also referred to as the Sephira, the giver of Wisdom. The name Sephira has been associated with the feminine divine figure in many cultures and spiritual traditions, a symbol of wisdom, beauty, and creativity.
data.spiritual_significance: Sephira represents the divine feminine, the spiritual wisdom, and the deep connection to the natural world. She embodies the nurturing, compassionate, and intuitive qualities of the feminine, and a reminder of the balance between the material and spiritual realms. Sephira's name carries the power of transformation, education, and understanding, providing a source of spiritual guidance and enlightenment.

In Wicca and Wiccan practices, it is a Hebrew name for the Goddess associated with the sphere of the Moon, Beauty, Form, and Balance. It may be also associated with Venus and the planetary sphere of Venus, as well as the Tree of Life's Sephira of Beauty. In occult and esoteric studies, Sephirra can refer to the Sephira of the same name in the Tree of Life, associated with the realm of the astral world, the spirit of the planet Venus, and the goddess of Love, Beauty and Harmony. In role-playing games and virtual worlds, Sephirra may be the name of a character, NPC, or location, representing the Goddess of Love, Beauty, and Harmony, or a powerful sorceress or priestess.
